questions.q: Why does presenting to Priya and Casey together differ from briefing each separately?
options: It doesn't — the content would be identical either way
One account of the project has to satisfy both an IT Manager's reliability/budget lens and a VP of Engineering's process lens at the same time, in the same room
Casey should receive a different set of facts than Priya
Group meetings require less preparation than one-on-ones
questions.explain: The two stakeholders care about the same project through different lenses, so one honest account needs to answer both at once, not a quietly tailored version for each.

questions.q: How does Theo open the presentation?
options: By narrating events in the exact chronological order they happened
By leading with the current outcome — the platform is live, and two issues were found and fixed before causing real damage
By apologizing extensively before explaining anything
By only discussing the successful parts and omitting both issues
questions.explain: Leading with the current state and the fact that both issues are already resolved gives both listeners the headline before the supporting detail.

questions.q: What does Theo emphasize specifically for Priya as IT Manager?
options: The exact Terraform syntax used in the fix
The cost impact (~40% over budget for about three weeks) and that the pipeline now prevents that specific mistake from shipping silently again
Nothing related to cost, since that's not her concern
Only the bucket policy issue, omitting the cost issue entirely
questions.explain: The cost figure and the fact it's now guarded against are what map directly onto an IT Manager's actual area of responsibility.

questions.q: What does Theo emphasize specifically for Casey as VP of Engineering?
options: That both issues were caught through review discipline, not luck, and are now automated checks in CI/CD
Only the dollar amount of the cost overshoot
That the engineering team should be reprimanded
Technical minutiae irrelevant to process or practice
questions.explain: The process point -- that disciplined review and now automation caught these, not luck -- is what matters most at a VP of Engineering's altitude.

questions.q: Why does the timing of this disclosure (after both fixes and the guardrail already shipped) matter?
options: It doesn't matter when Theo discloses this, only that he eventually does
Bringing a self-found, self-fixed, already-guarded issue to stakeholders voluntarily is a fundamentally different and more trust-building conversation than waiting for it to be discovered externally
Theo should have disclosed it immediately upon noticing the cost anomaly, before investigating
Disclosure timing has no bearing on how it's received
questions.explain: Voluntarily disclosing a found-and-fixed issue, with a preventive mechanism already in place, is what actually earns trust rather than spending it.
